steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease two cookie sheets.
Whisk flour, cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, nutmeg, cloves, and salt together in a medium bowl until well combined.
Cream sugar and butter together in a large bowl until fluffy, 2 to 3 minutes. Add pumpkin, egg, and vanilla extract; beat until creamy. Mix in flour mixture until combined.
Drop tablespoonfuls of cookie dough onto the prepared pans; flatten slightly.
Bake in the preheated oven until centers set, 15 to 20 minutes, switching racks halfway through. Transfer cookies to a wire rack; cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes.
Stir confectioners' sugar, milk, butter, and vanilla extract togeher in a large bowl until smooth. Add more milk as needed to reach desired drizzling consistency.
Drizzle icing over cooled cookies with a fork.

raw_recipe.headline: Iced Pumpkin Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This iced pumpkin cookies recipe makes soft pumpkin cookies, perfectly spiced with warming cinnamon, nutmeg, and clove spice, then drizzled with icing.

video.description: Pumpkin cookies with cream cheese frosting are always a hit, especially around Halloween and Thanksgiving. And when they're soft, moist, and topped with a sweet cream cheese frosting? Well, they're impossible to resist! Serve the recipe in this video with a little frosting if you want.

review.reviewBody: I make these every year around the holidays - people love them. Do not store them in an airtight container though - they have a lot of moisture from the pumpkin and get moist and mushy. They stay great out on the counter for days. Delicious w/ coffee!

These cookies are superb. Soft and cakelike, not at all dense or sticky. The take on a beautiful shape while baking. I replaced 1/2 cup of the white sugar with light brown sugar and used 1 1/2 teaspoons of cinnamon and 1 1/2 teaspoons of pumpkin pie spice instead of the spices listed (what I happened to have on hand). Try adding a little cinnamon to the icing--it looks beautiful. So good! Thanks for the recipe!

This recipe is very good. However, I needed to make a few adjudments. I followed the recipe exactly and the end product was this: a cookie that was bready and not sweet like a cookie should be. So for my second batch I added more pumpkin and more sugar and decreased the baking time to 12 minutes. Also, since I'm not a big fan of icing on cookies, I ommitted the icing. Viola! A perfect pumpkin spice cookie =)

Years ago I gave this wonderful recipe to a former friend of mine who owns a chain of 17 deli-restaurants in our area. Customers LOVE this cake-like cookie. It is so popular it is sold year-round. Skip the glaze and use a cream cheese icing instead. Delicious! *****UPDATE 2011***** Apparently these are THE most popular cookies sold in this business and they sell out daily. If anyone is wondering, the initials of this business are "C.B" and it is located in the mid-south.

For someone who has never liked pumpkin much these cookies are just pure DANGER!
Not only was the wonderful 'Fall' aroma wonderful through the house ... but the cookies are extremely tasty.
I can just tell I'll be making these quite a bit this season ... maybe even still this week again ... I'd love to share it with everyone!
Not too bad in the fat/calorie content area either ... especially since I used margarine instead of butter and they still turned out awesome!
Thankyou so much Gina for changing my idea of pumpkin!

I’ve made these several times now. Only change I made was that I wasn’t paying attention and used the whole 15 oz can of pumpkin rather than 1 cup called for, but the cookies still turned out great! They make wonderfully soft delicious cookies that aren’t overly sweet. The batter is fairly thick and sticky, and the cookies don’t really spread out when baking, so I’ve made these as drop cookies, that I slightly flattened with a cup that I had coated the bottom with sugar, I’ve also just dropped spoonfuls of the batter and then sprinkled a cinnamon sugar blend over the top, and I’ve put the batter into a zip top bag, snipped a wide opening in the corner and piped these out into donut shapes (making sure to pipe thickly). They all still baked in about the same amount of time 12-15 minutes. I’ve also added chocolate chips to the batter, and those cookies were an even bigger hit! This recipe is definitely a keeper!

Really good!! Love how I'd already have most ingredients on-hand and don't have to break the bank for a batch of cookies. The reviews are generally spot on, these are very cakey and good. I also followed the comments where I used 15oz of pumpkin, split the sugar as half light brown and half white, and used heaping table/tea spoons of the spices for a lil extra flavor. As warned in the comments, the pumpkin makes the dough a bit stickier, but I just threw it in the fridge for a bit and shaped them as best as I could when cold. They don't spread nearly at all (good if you wanna do cut-outs too!!). I skipped the icing since I didn't wanna buy confectioner's sugar and bought a cream cheese icing. I melted it for like 5-8 seconds in the microwave, mixed with some cinnamon, and drizzled it over. Was a hit! Definitely a keeper.

Loved these. They worked great with King Arthur gluten free 1 to 1 flour. I halved the recipe but had a derp moment and forgot to halve the pumpkin and they still turned out wonderful. I used mini semi sweet chocolate chips in the batter instead of frosting. I love that these are light and fluffy and not overwhelmingly sweet.

Technically, I didn't follow the recipe, but I used it as a reference for a quick change up. I used 1 stick of soft butter, 1 egg, a 15 oz can of pumpkin puree, and a package of Miss Jones pumpkin bread mix. I also added about 1/4 c sugar. Baked a little longer than the 20 minutes, because otherwise the inside was a little tasting of raw pumpkin. But I turned off the oven before I popped the trays back in for about 8 minutes. I used a canned cream cheese icing, and the cookies tasted great. I also cook on parchment, not greased pan

Perfect! I did double the spices because I love cinnamon, cloves, etc. I cut the sugar down by a little more than 1/2 a cup, using around 3/4 cup. I made them smaller using a small cookie scoop and baked for 11 minutes. They're soft and delicious and perfect for my kids' school's fall bake sale.

I loved the way these turned out! At first when the batter was done I was a bit nervous as it was a bit liquid-y and nothing like I've ever made before. I really didn't want to waste it so I tried it out by taking a spoon of the batter and putting on the plate and putting in the microwave for a minute. I was super excited and it turned out great. So I then put them in the oven for about 16ish minutes. Took them out and made the glaze. I cut the glaze recipe in half as it seemed like a lot of glaze for about 25 cookies. I didn't use butter in the glaze and it turned about delish. I had everyone try them and they all loved them, even if its the middle of summer ! Thanks for the recipe- BlinkReagan
Great recipe took about the amount of time suggested. It turned out great and my daughters love these cookies. They eat them up every time and get their pumpkin with them.

Love. Love. Love this Recipe. During the holidays I gift them to friends and family. On the recommendation of other reviewer's, I added half brown sugar for the 1.5 c. Sugar. The icing I only made half and had enough to drizzle on all the cookies. This is my favorite cookie recipe!
I absolutely loved this recipe and so did my family members
turned out soft fluffy and full of flavor.
I get asked for these year round.
I made this for the first time and used gluten free ingredients. They turned out great. I cheated with the frosting and used a cream cheese flavor can. Im taking them to a potluck at work.

My adult kids have always liked pumpkin muffins, but these cookies are their new favorites! I follow the cookie recipe to the letter, but after they’re cool, I put a small swirl of melted chocolate on top. I use Ghirardelli dark chocolate melts. However, these cookies are so soft and flavorful, they would easily stand alone without any icing! Thanks for sharing.❤️
Easy recipe and very tasty. I added a 1/4 c brown sugar along with the butter, sugar, vanilla and egg mix.
These cookies are tender and have a great fall flavor ❤️. They’re excellent even without the icing.
